items.title: AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service
items.summary: AWS has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for AWS Connect Customer. This recognition marks an important milestone for our team, and it reflects years of work pushing on what’s possible in customer experience.

items.title: Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs
items.summary: Seekable OCI (SOCI) indexing for Amazon SageMaker AI training and processing jobs takes full container image download off the critical path. SageMaker AI lazy-loads your image to start containers in seconds instead of minutes, with no changes to your job definition. See the benchmarks and how to adopt it.

items.title: Fix evaluation bias to unlock better models on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Property Finder found that 96.8% of their vision-AI evaluation labels were inherited from the incumbent model, hiding its true accuracy. See how they built unbiased ground truth, applied evolutionary prompt optimization, and selected a more accurate, cost-effective model on Amazon Bedrock, cutting cost by 86% across 11 image-quality attributes.

items.title: Exowatt beats frontier models on accuracy with SageMaker serverless model customization
items.summary: In this post, we show how Exowatt used Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization to build a repeatable AI pipeline that produces task-specific fine-tuned models for two deployment targets, edge and cloud, achieving higher accuracy than frontier models at up to 49x lower cost.

items.title: Fleet-wide computer vision lifecycle at the edge with SageMaker SDK v3
items.summary: Fleet-wide computer vision needs a model per camera, not one model for the whole fleet. This post presents a working Amazon SageMaker SDK v3 reference architecture that trains, quality-gates, compiles per-camera models with SageMaker Neo, and versions thousands of them, with an AWS Step Functions layer pacing fleet-scale retraining within account quotas.

items.title: Groundhog Day for AI agents: Prompt caching patterns for using OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Every time an agent takes a step, it re-reads its entire context before acting. Here is how prompt caching for OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock lets your agent remember, cutting input cost and latency without resending the same tools, instructions, and history every turn.

items.title: Build agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with CDK
items.summary: Build enterprise agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with the AWS CDK: an agent that routes across two knowledge bases, retrieves through the AgentCore Gateway, and returns grounded, cited answers, with seven layers of observability and both on-demand and continuous evaluation, all deployed as a single CDK application.

items.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide
items.summary: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI trains models on the outcome of a whole multi-step task rather than labeled steps. This hands-on guide walks the full pipeline using Wordle: deploying the agent and reward on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preparing the dataset, training, and evaluating at serving settings.

items.title: Orchestrating SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling with AWS CDK
items.summary: Updating a SageMaker AI endpoint that has Application Auto Scaling registered makes AWS CloudFormation and AWS CDK deployments fail. This post shows how to build a reusable AWS CDK construct with CloudFormation custom resources that deregisters and re-registers auto scaling automatically, so you can update the endpoint and its scaling in a single deployment.

items.title: Visualize points and routes with GeoJSON in Amazon Quick Sight layer maps
items.summary: Amazon Quick Sight layer maps now support Point and LineString geometry from the same GeoJSON workflow, so you can plot store locations and the routes between them. This post covers the dataset and GeoJSON structure layer maps require, when to choose points or lines, and techniques for viewport control, layering geometries, and dynamic GeoJSON updates.
